C-33.Name: New app icon: highlighted pilcrow ¶ with macOS 26 dark and tinted appearances
C-33.Summary: G2 of the MarkView gap plan. Replace the circle-with-cyan-M icon with the pilcrow family chosen on 2026-10-14 after three design rounds and independent 5-angle reviews (canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/4A5sHFVmv4ano8MTxZeaY2): a custom-drawn ¶ whose D-shaped bowl is filled highlighter yellow (#FFCF1A) and outlined in ink (#17191E) on warm paper (#F5EFE4). The icon ships as a classic icns (macOS 12–25, Windows/Linux sets) and as an Icon Composer .icon compiled by actool into Assets.car with CFBundleIconName, so macOS 26 renders the Liquid Glass default, dark and tinted appearances. A prior-art / trademark similarity search runs before the artwork is frozen.

Problem.Description: The current icon is a circle (not the macOS squircle) with a cyan "M" that sits in the competitor M-letter cluster (MWeb, MD Editor Pro, One Markdown, Marked); it has no dark/tinted variants.
Problem.RootCause: Legacy icon from the alpha period; no icon system.
Problem.Evidence: src-tauri/icons/icon.icns; competitor wall and reviews on the canvas.

Goals.R-1: Master artwork as SVG sources in assets/icon/ (light, dark, tinted reference, 16 px master, layer SVGs for Icon Composer), drawn as paths — no font glyphs.
Goals.R-2: src-tauri/icons/* regenerated: icon.icns from a hand-assembled iconset (16 px uses the 16 px master), icon.ico, 32x32/128x128/128x128@2x PNGs and the Windows Square*/StoreLogo PNGs from a full-bleed variant.
Goals.R-3: assets/icon/AppIcon.icon (Icon Composer format: background fill with dark specialization, bowl and ink layers) compiled by actool into src-tauri/icons/Assets.car; tauri.conf bundle.macOS.files ships it as Contents/Resources/Assets.car and src-tauri/Info.plist sets CFBundleIconName=AppIcon. MAS packaging keeps working.
Goals.R-4: Site favicon/logo (site/public) and README/landing references switch to the new mark.
Goals.R-5: Prior-art similarity research recorded in this change (Amendments) before release; artwork adjusted if a medium-or-higher risk is found.

Constraints.Constraint: No tag or release without an explicit command; the icon ships with 2.3.0 together with the new store screenshots.
Drawn paths only; no third-party glyphs or assets.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Landing-page colour system rework beyond swapping the logo (follow-up).
Quick Look extension icon (separate Xcode target).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Built .app shows the new icon in Finder/Dock; on macOS 26 Assets.car contains AppIcon with dark and tinted renditions (assetutil --info).
cargo/renderer suites and CI green; release preflight unaffected.
Prior-art report attached; no medium+ risk left unaddressed.

C-33.VerificationIntent: actool compile log + assetutil dump of Assets.car; local debug .app bundle inspection (Info.plist CFBundleIconName, Resources/Assets.car); visual check of icns sizes; CI green.

Amendment.Item: Prior-art search (≈1,550 App Store icons across 29 terms, web, trademark sources): no registered pilcrow figurative mark for software; the bare ¶ skeleton is generic (SF Symbols paragraphsign, Material format_paragraph, Lucide/Tabler pilcrow). Closest look-alike: Prosely: Markdown Editor (Mac App Store, released 2026-09-15, id6805104509) — same D-bowl + two equal square stems; risk medium for the round-3 shape.

Round 4 shape change to break that silhouette, confirmed by an independent critique: chisel-tip highlighter bowl (slanted left edge), nib-cut stem feet, right stem ~9% shorter; a hand-placed 16 px master and an enlarged-glyph rendition for 32/64 px. Yellow / ink / paper palette kept (unique among the look-alikes). SF Symbols are never traced; all paths are drawn in assets/icon/gen.py.

Icon Composer: layer fills recolour every shape, so the bowl outline is an evenodd ring rather than a stroke; tinted appearance pins ink to white and the bowl to mid grey. ictool previews of default/dark/tinted/clear all read as ¶.

Review follow-up: paper is a #FAF6EE → #EFE7D8 gradient in the classic art (solid #F5EFE4 in the Icon Composer fill); Assets.car is ~1.8 MB (≈12% of the 15 MB footprint target, accepted); icon.ico now stores PNG frames (305 KB → 14 KB); build.sh records Assets.car.sources.sha256 and icon-assets.test.js fails on .icon edits without a rebuild; R-4 is partial — logo-96px replaced, the landing page itself moves to C-35.

Pre-release gate (owned by C-23): validate the MAS .pkg with Transporter / altool (CFBundleIconName makes App Store Connect require AppIcon in Assets.car incl. 512/1024 renditions — present per assetutil).
